name: Audit Defence and Controversy
title: Audit Defence and Controversy
answer: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of preparing for, responding to, and resolving disputes with tax authorities over positions that involve AI systems, data, or automated decisions. It includes transfer pricing for AI-related intangibles, R&D credits for model development, characterization of AI services, and documentation of algorithms used in tax calculations. The page sits within tax and jurisdictional compliance because AI creates new audit triggers around data location, profit attribution, and evidentiary standards.

sections.body: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of preparing for, responding to, and resolving disputes with tax authorities over positions that involve AI systems, data, or automated decisions. It includes transfer pricing for AI-related intangibles, R&D credits for model development, characterization of AI services, and documentation of algorithms used in tax calculations. The page sits within tax and jurisdictional compliance because AI creates new audit triggers around data location, profit attribution, and evidentiary standards.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the same document management, e-discovery, and workflow tools used in tax controversy, now extended to handle model cards, training data logs, and version histories. Practitioners rely on secure repositories that preserve the chain of custody for AI artifacts, plus tax controversy platforms that track correspondence, deadlines, and issue logs. Cloud-based case management and encrypted file sharing are standard, with some teams using AI-assisted document review to sort large volumes of audit requests.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Tax professionals map each AI-related position to the underlying facts, such as where models were trained, where data was stored, and which entity owns the intellectual property. They prepare contemporaneous documentation that links business purpose, functional analysis, and economic substance to the AI system's design and use. During an audit, they respond to information document requests by producing model documentation, training data descriptions, and decision logs, and they test the tax authority's technical assumptions against the actual system behavior.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Audit defence turns on the ability to prove who did what, when, and with which data. Taxpayers need clear ownership records for models and datasets, access controls that show who could change a system, and retention policies that preserve the version used in the tax year under review. Risk arises when an AI system is a black box to the tax team, when training data crosses borders without clear transfer pricing, or when an auditor challenges the reliability of automated outputs. No page here is legal advice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Tax authorities are building their own AI audit tools to select cases, spot anomalies, and reconstruct taxpayer positions, which will raise the bar for documentation quality. Expect more controversy over the location of value creation in AI supply chains, the deductibility of model training costs, and the evidentiary weight of machine-generated logs. Practitioners will need to treat model provenance and audit trails as first-class tax records, not afterthoughts, and to prepare for disputes that hinge on technical details of training runs and inference.
